_comment: credential-root-grants.v1.json — one ROOT GRANT per provider that offers a non-interactive mint API (Joe's ruling 2026-10-12, decision cbe91287-10a2-48d0-bda7-3b1784b4bb93: credential minting must not require him). Joe places each root grant ONCE with its one_time_command; from then on ops/credential-mint.py (nightly step 'credential mint') mints, verifies, installs, stores and revokes every child named under `children`, rotating each `rotate_within_days` before its ttl runs out. A credential this file cannot mint is marked `holder_only` with its reason in ops/config/credential-inventory.v1.json; the inventory and this file are checked against each other by lib/credential_mint.load_plan(). NEVER put a secret VALUE here. Every endpoint below is the provider's documented control-plane API; none was called while this file was written (no live provider call from a build seat), so the first night after a grant is placed is the first live exercise, and verify-before-store keeps the existing credential in place if any call is refused.

grants.name: cloudflare
grants.scope: A Cloudflare USER API token (My Profile > API Tokens > Create Custom Token) carrying exactly one permission: User > API Tokens > Edit ('API Tokens Write'). It can create and delete the same user's API tokens and nothing else. Children are minted under /user/tokens, so they are user-owned and the existing /user/tokens/verify probes keep working unchanged.
grants.verify: GET https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/user/tokens/verify with the token as Bearer; HTTP 200 and result.status == 'active'. Read-only.

params._note: account_id is the CARR account mcp-server/wrangler.toml deploys to. Each child is scoped to that account only, with the two permission groups the hand-made deploy token carried (Workers Scripts:Edit + Account Settings:Read); group names are resolved to ids at mint time from GET /user/tokens/permission_groups, and an unresolvable name refuses the mint.

grants.name: neon
grants.scope: A Neon ORGANIZATION API key for org org-dry-dew-75906281 (Organization settings > API keys, created by an org admin). It can create and revoke that organization's API keys and read its projects; it is not tied to Joe's personal account.
grants.verify: GET https://console.neon.tech/api/v2/projects?org_id=org-dry-dew-75906281 with the key as Bearer; any 2xx. Read-only. The same question tools/rotate-credential.py and the neon-api-key health probe ask.

params._note: The organization tools/db-tap.py and tools/rotate-credential.py pin. Children are organization API keys (POST /organizations/{org_id}/api_keys), revoked by id (DELETE /organizations/{org_id}/api_keys/{key_id}).

grants.name: openai
grants.scope: An OpenAI ORGANIZATION ADMIN key (platform.openai.com > Organization settings > Admin keys). It can create and delete project service accounts, each of which carries its own project API key. tools/system_costs.py already reads billing with this same name, so one placed key serves both.
grants.verify: GET https://api.openai.com/v1/organization/projects?limit=1 with the admin key as Bearer; HTTP 200. Children are verified with GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models; HTTP 200. Read-only.

params._note: Children are service accounts of the project named here (POST /v1/organization/projects/{project_id}/service_accounts), found by name and created once if absent, revoked by deleting the service account. A minted key is installed into Codex with `codex login --with-api-key` (value on stdin, never argv), which moves Codex from ChatGPT-subscription auth to metered API-key auth on that machine.

grants.name: xai
grants.scope: An xAI MANAGEMENT API key (console.x.ai > Settings > Management keys), which can create and delete the team's API keys.
grants.deferred: Nothing in the inventory consumes an xAI API key: Grok runs through the Grok CLI on a grok.com OAuth login (grok-cli-auth, holder_only, `grok login` offers only --oauth and --device-auth). Placing a management key today would mint children nobody reads, so it is not asked for. The first API consumer adds a child here, a store_name in lib/token_store.py, and an adapter in lib/credential_mint.py.

grants.name: github-app
grants.scope: The CARR GitHub App private key (app 5199739, installed on jbookout/carr-system), at ~/.config/carr/<key_file from ops/config/github-app.json>.
grants.system_command: lib/github_app_token.gh_env() — already derives a fresh installation token for every background gh call
grants.verify: Presence of the key file only (os.path.exists, never opened by the mint path). lib/github_app_token.py proves it on use: a JWT exchange for an installation token.
